notes.1i: This question was straightforward for the majority of candidates who frequently gained full marks. Errors were usually due to the use of h = 20 instead of h = 20 sin 30 leading to 1600 J, or the use o o of cos 30 instead of sin 30 leading to 1386 J.
notes.1iii: Candidates needed to distinguish between force and work done. Some candidates calculated the difference between the total work done and the gain in potential energy (346 J), omitting to divide by the distance travelled in order to find the frictional force. Others found the total force (57.3 N) but omitted to subtract the component of weight down the plane. Answer: 800 J 17.3 N
notes.2i: Nearly all candidates applied constant acceleration formulae accurately although a few found only one of the two quantities.
notes.2iii: Part (ii) proved to be more challenging. Candidates attempted to form an equation in t but the equation was often incorrect due to the different starting times for Alan and Ben. It was common to see equations such as 4t = 15 + 6(t – 5) using a 5 second time difference for the constant speeds rather than a 10 second time difference. Answer: 15 m 6 ms 90 m �PAGE�42
notes.3: This question was answered very well by most candidates and fully correct solutions were common. Candidates knew how to resolve forces in equilibrium to form simultaneous equations in P and θ. The few errors that occurred were usually due to a trigonometric slip when resolving, or difficulty in solving the simultaneous equations. Accuracy was not usually an issue, but candidates should beware of approximating early e.g. sin θ = 12.9/13.7 leading to θ = 70.3 instead of 70.8. A significant number of candidates found horizontal and vertical components rather than forming simultaneous equations and were then able to obtain P and θ successfully using Pythagoras’ Theorem and trigonometry. Answer: 13.7 70.8
notes.4: Most candidates attempted to resolve the forces parallel and perpendicular to the plane as expected and often found both values of X accurately and concisely. X was sometimes shown acting down the plane, and occasionally shown in a horizontal direction instead of parallel to the plane, leading to a more complex situation. Those who started with X acting down the plane either stated X = –23.1, usually with no explanation for the negative value, or solved their equation making a sign error and concluding X = 23.1 as given in the question. Some candidates found only one answer rather than a least and a greatest value for X. A few stated X = 15 g sin 20 , assuming no friction despite the rough plane. Those who attempted to form inequalities rather than equations often experienced difficulty with the direction of the inequality, concluding e.g. X ≤ 23.1. Answer: 79.5
notes.5: This question differentiated well between candidates with most able to answer part (i) and a variety of errors seen in parts (ii) and (iii).
notes.5i: P = DF × v was usually applied accurately with a driving force of 650 N for the situation of constant speed. A few candidates erroneously included the weight e.g. v = 20000/14000 or v = 20000/(14000 + 650).
notes.5iii: Whilst nearly all candidates calculated 80% of the power found in part (ii) as required, many oversimplified the new situation of acceleration down the hill, omitting either the weight component or the resisting force or both. Thus, common incorrect answers were a = 0.293 ms from 21200/20 – 650 = 1400 a, and a = 0.757 ms from 21200/20 = 1400 a. Some candidates found a deceleration, (a = –1.14 ms ), following a sign error in 21200/20 – 650 – 1400 g sin θ = 1400 a suggesting uphill motion. –1 –2 Answer: 30.8 ms 26500 W 1.72 ms

notes.key_messages:
• Non-exact numerical answers are required correct to three significant figures as stated on the
question paper. Candidates are also reminded to maintain sufficient accuracy in their working to
achieve this level of accuracy in their final answers.
• Candidates are reminded of the importance of a clear and complete force diagram in problem
solving and a consideration of all forces when resolving or when writing down equations of motion.
notes.general_comments:
This examination proved to be straightforward for many candidates. There was much work of a very high
standard including many excellent, well presented scripts. Question 3 was found to be the easiest question
whilst Question 2(ii), Question 5(iii) and Question 7(ii) provided the most challenge.
